messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: selectInput enhancements?
parts:
Hm, that is very slow. Here's an example app:

library(shiny)

n_choices <- 5000

runApp(list(
  ui = pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel(""),
    sidebarPanel(
      uiOutput("ui")
    ),
    mainPanel(
      verbatimTextOutput("text")
    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$ui <- renderUI({
      choices <- paste0("choice", 1:n_choices)
      names(choices) <- choices

      selectInput("select", "Select:", multiple = TRUE, choices = choices)
    })
    
    output$text <- renderText({
      input$select
    })
  }
))



And here's code that illustrates the problem more directly:
  n_choices <- 5000
  choices <- paste0("choice", 1:n_choices)
  names(choices) <- choices
  s <- selectInput("select", "Select:", multiple = TRUE, choices = choices)


I'll look into speeding it up.

-Winston

On Mon, Jun 17, 2013 at 6:24 PM, Andrew Clark <scott.r...@gmail.com> wrote:
a) It only occurs when multiple=TRUE. When there is a selected with multiple=FALSE then only the one option is shown. With the former, the selectInput opens up
with a choice of however many there is room to show but starts from the top of the list rather than, say, the first of the selected. 

b) 5,000 seems to take about 45sec. I get round it by initially loading a subsample of more likely selections and allowing users the option - via a radio button - to load all 


On Monday, 17 June 2013 15:54:12 UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
If I understand a) correctly, we don't really have control over this--it's up to the browser how the select element actually behaves.

For b), how large are we talking about?

b) Faint hope, but is there anyway to speed up populating a selectInput for large datasets.
